original_question: (V. M. Kopytov, N. Ya. Medvedev). Is it true that the lattice of rightrelatively convex subgroups of a right-orderable group is distributive if and only if it is a chain?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.148 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", with the definition of "right-relatively convex" supplied immediately before in Problem 21.147.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact mathematical target very closely: it identifies the correct class of groups (right-orderable groups), the correct subgroups (right-relatively convex subgroups), and the precise lattice-theoretic question asked in the paper (whether distributivity occurs exactly in the chain case). It also correctly attributes the problem to V. M. Kopytov and N. Ya. Medvedev.
missing_details: The question should explicitly fix a right-orderable group G whose right-relatively convex subgroups are being considered.
It should import the paper's definition from Problem 21.147: a subgroup H ≤ G is right-relatively convex if it is convex under some right ordering of G.
To be fully stand-alone, it should unpack "convex": for some right-invariant total order ≤ on G, whenever h1 ≤ g ≤ h2 with h1,h2 in H, one has g in H.
It should make explicit that the relevant lattice is the inclusion-ordered lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of G, and that "chain" means totally ordered by inclusion.
refined_question: Let G be a right-orderable group. Call a subgroup H ≤ G right-relatively convex if there exists a right-invariant total order ≤ on G such that H is convex with respect to ≤, i.e. whenever h1 ≤ g ≤ h2 with h1,h2 ∈ H, then g ∈ H. Is the inclusion-ordered lattice of right-relatively convex subgroups of G distributive if and only if it is a chain?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper's official open problem 21.148. The only substantive context missing for a stand-alone formulation is the definition of "right-relatively convex," which is given immediately beforehand in Problem 21.147. Since arXiv:1401.0300 is the Kourovka Notebook, the relevant target here is this numbered open problem rather than a conjecture/proposition/theorem elsewhere in the paper.
